ov: Six species of spotted carnivorous marsupials from Australia and New Guinea, also once called native cats. They are nocturnal and mostly solitary. All species have declined since European settlement, and the eastern quoll vanished from mainland Australia in the 1960s.
wt: 300 g to 7 kg, depending on the species
rg: Mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea, now in much smaller areas than before.
df: Small species: insects, birds, frogs, lizards and fruit. Larger ones: birds, reptiles and mammals such as possums.
fx: A newborn quoll is the size of a grain of rice, and a female may give birth to up to 30 but has only six or seven teats.
